records.title: A Local Law in relation to requiring the commissioner of health and mental hygiene to establish and operate a pilot program providing free mental health services to children who have been returned to their home following a removal, and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon the expiration thereof
agencies_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

program_breakdowns.program: Mental Health Services Pilot Program - Social Workers
program_breakdowns.description: Hiring of two social workers to operate a pilot program providing free mental health services to children reunified with families following ACS removal, serving 50 eligible families.
program_breakdowns.offset_notes: Annual salary per social worker estimated at $72,495 with 50% fringe rate ($108,743 per year per position); prorated in FY27 and FY30

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues as a result of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: The Council estimates that total cost of the enactment of this legislation would be $652,455 to hire two social workers to fulfill this legislation's requirements for the three-year period of the pilot. The annual salary for each social worker is estimated to be $72,495 with a 50 percent fringe rate for a total cost of $108,743 per year for each position. Because this legislation is anticipated to be effective for only a portion of Fiscal 2027, the prorated costs in that year are estimated to be $159,688. For Fiscals 2028 and 2029, the cost is estimated to be $217,485 per year. In Fiscal 2030 the cost is estimated to be $57,797, which is prorated for the portion of the year the program would be effective before it is deemed repealed. The Council estimates the pilot program would operate with 50 slots for eligible families and the two social workers to administer services. Based on the Council's analysis of current ACS operations and understanding of the removal process, youth who have been removed from their families and then reunified are typically already participating in court-mandated or other ACS-provided mental health services as part of the reunification process and the demand for this program is likely to only require the hiring of two additional social workers for the duration of the pilot.
records.omb_estimate_notes: The Office of Management and Budget did not provide an estimate.

records.title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring all schools to stock airway clearance devices, and to repeal section two of such local law upon the expiration thereof

program_breakdowns.description: One-time procurement and distribution of FDA-approved airway clearance devices (one case per school) to 2,734 schools.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is estimated that there would be no impact on revenues resulting from the enactment of this legislation. The Office of Management and Budget (OMB)'s estimate of this legislation's impact on the City's revenues is consistent with the Council's estimate.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: It is estimated that there would be an impact on expenditures resulting from the enactment of this legislation. The Department of Education (DOE) would need to provide airway clearance devices to 2,734 schools, including public, charter and private schools as of the 2024-2025 school year. Airway clearance devices would be defined by the proposed legislation as a medical device registered as a class II acute upper airway obstruction device with the United States Food and Drug Administration. Class II acute upper airway obstruction devices are not FDA approved to be sold over the counter. Since these devices are single-use and the legislation does not explicitly cite the number of devices per school, our estimate assumes that each school would be required to stock multiple airway clearance devices. The cost for a case of FDA approved devices is approximately $2,000. To stock all schools with a case of airway clearance devices would result in a $5,468,000 one-time expense in the fiscal year that the legislation takes effect. OMB's estimate of this legislation's impact on the City's expenditures is consistent with the Council's estimate insofar as OMB estimates some cost, however OMB did not provide a specific estimate.
records.omb_estimate_notes: OMB provided an estimate confirming that some cost would be incurred, consistent with the Council's estimate, though OMB did not provide a specific dollar amount.
